page: Amazon Web Services r7g.12xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and custom AWS Graviton3 processors. Built on the ARMv8 64-bit architecture using Neoverse-V1 cores, this instance features 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs clocked at 2.6 GHz, operating with one thread per core. The memory subsystem delivers 384.0 GB of RAM, sustaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB per core. The instance is not equipped with discrete GPUs and provides no bundled local NVMe storage, relying on external network storage. Network interfaces provide a baseline throughput of 22 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate exceptional memory and multi-core parallel processing efficiency. In the PassMark memory suite, the system attained a top-tier score of 3,165.6, backed by uncached memory read bandwidth of 253.07 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 115.25 GB/sec. Parallel CPU throughput showed strong scores in stress-ng multi-core tests (73,472.18) and Geekbench multi-core performance (19,239.0), including solid compiler efficiency with Clang (52,625.0). In operational database testing, the instance achieved strong marks for database operations (31,334.79) and maintained 77.38 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads. Conversely, single-threaded throughput ranks in the middle tier, with Geekbench single-core at 1,521.0 and stress-ng single-core at 1,532.78, reflecting standard baseline clock frequencies.

Architecturally, the absence of simultaneous multithreading ensures that each vCPU is backed by a physical execution pipeline, avoiding noisy-neighbor core contention. A trade-off to consider is the requirement of ARM-compatible software stacks, as well as the complete reliance on remote block storage due to the lack of integrated local disks. The high RAM capacity paired with an efficient Graviton3 architecture yields strong cost efficiency per unit of memory compared to legacy x86 architectures.

The r7g.12xlarge instance is best suited for memory-intensive enterprise workloads that do not require local ephemeral scratch space. Target deployments include in-memory databases like Redis and Memcached, distributed caching tiers, large-scale relational database engines, high-throughput static web serving, and memory-bound analytics pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r7g.12xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro-based cloud server powered by AWS Graviton3 Neoverse-V1 ARM64 processors. It is configured with 48 dedicated physical cores running at 2.6 GHz, delivering 48 vCPUs with 1 thread per core, paired with 384.0 GB of system memory at an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio. The instance includes 22 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no integrated local storage, and features no dedicated GPUs. In benchmarks, the server ranks in the top tier for memory performance and demonstrates strong multi-core execution across stress-ng, Geekbench compilation, and Redis SET transactions reaching 77.38 million ops/sec. While single-thread performance is modest, its resource density and architectural isolation provide high efficiency for memory-heavy operations, distributed caching, enterprise in-memory databases, and high-concurrency web tiers.
